# Separating Computation from I/O

A function that computes *and* prints can only be tested by capturing stdout. A function that returns
a value can be tested by comparing it. That is the entire argument, and
[[python-programming-laboratories]] applies it as a rule rather than a preference.

## The three applications in `weblog`

**`stats` never prints.** Every aggregation returns a data structure; the CLI layer decides how to
render it. The stated reason is testability, and the test suite is the proof — the stats tests assert
on returned values with no capsys anywhere.

**Config is read inside `main()`, never at import time.** Import-time config reading means importing
the module has a side effect: it touches the filesystem, can raise, and pins the config path before
any caller gets a say. Deferring it to `main()` keeps import pure, so tests can import the module and
inject their own config. `Config` fronts both JSON and INI behind one interface, and a `ConfigError`
is raised at load rather than at first use — failing where the mistake is, not three call frames
later.

**Paging checks `isatty()`.** The program pages output when a human is watching and streams plainly
when piped. The computation is identical either way; only the presentation layer inspects the
environment. This is the same separation pushed all the way to the terminal boundary.

## Why it compounds

The nine labs that read the same access log are thin scripts precisely *because* the computation has
no I/O baked in — see [[extract-the-shared-core]]. Had `stats` printed, every lab would have needed
its own copy with different formatting, and the shared core would never have been extractable.

The same discipline is what makes [[common-log-format-parsing]] testable: `iter_entries` yields
objects, `ParseReport` accumulates counts, and nothing in the parsing path writes to a stream.

## The general shape

- **Pure core, imperative shell.** Decisions and calculations in functions that take data and return
  data; reading, writing, printing and clock-checking at the edges.
- **Return, don't render.** `image_ratio` in lab 11 returns `None` rather than printing a zero — the
  caller decides what "no data" looks like.
- **Fail at the boundary.** Validate on load, so the pure core can assume well-formed input.
